title: Universal Life Insurance Owner Guide Table: Partial Withdrawal Limits and Default Federal Withholding
content:
Partial withdrawals from an Ashgrove Universal Life Insurance policy are bounded per tier by the figures below, and the tier's default federal withholding rate is the rate withheld on the taxable part of a distribution where the owner has not elected to have nothing withheld.

## Limits table

| Item | Lifetime Guarantee UL | Protection UL | Accumulation UL | Indexed UL Protect | Indexed UL Growth | Indexed UL Premier |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| First policy year in which a partial withdrawal may be taken | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| Smallest partial withdrawal | $500 | $500 | $500 | $500 | $500 | $500 |
| Fee deducted from the account value with each partial withdrawal | $25.00 | $25.00 | $25.00 | $25.00 | $25.00 | $25.00 |
| Most partial withdrawals in one policy year | 4 | 4 | 4 | 4 | 4 | 4 |
| Cash surrender value that must remain after a partial withdrawal | $500 | $500 | $500 | $500 | $500 | $500 |
| Default federal withholding rate on the taxable part of a distribution | 10% | 10% | 10% | 10% | 10% | 10% |

The withholding rate is 0.10 written as a decimal.

## Reading the table

- No partial withdrawal is taken in policy year 1; policy year 2 begins on the first policy anniversary.
- The fourth withdrawal of a policy year is within the limit; a fifth in the same policy year is not.
- The $500 floor on what remains is a cash surrender value figure, measured after the withdrawal.

## Hypothetical figures

On an Ashgrove Protection UL in policy year 3, a request for $400.00 is below the $500 smallest withdrawal, and a fifth withdrawal in the same policy year is above the limit of 4. Where a distribution has a taxable part of $2000.00 and the owner has not elected no withholding, 10% of it, $200.00, is withheld.
